title: Every path git tracks lands in one bucket with a reason

generate.repeat: Une ligne de remplissage pour dépasser le plafond du marcheur.
generate.why: Over the walker's 1 MiB default. Committing a megabyte of filler to measure a size cap would be a poor trade, so it is declared here instead of stored.

A symlink whose target is outside the repository. Generated rather than committed so the corpus stays checkout-portable, and pointed at a path that exists on every Linux and macOS — a BROKEN symlink is a different case, and one the walker currently drops silently.

Declared rather than committed, because a `.gitignore` stored inside the corpus applies to THIS repository too: `secrets/token.txt` would be silently dropped from the commit and the case would fail on a fresh clone. Keeping the whole ignored-but-tracked scenario in one place is also how it stays readable.

census.why: The ordinary case, present so the others are read against a baseline rather than in isolation.
Extensionless and readable. An extension-driven scanner skips it; PLAIN_TEXT_BASENAMES is why this one is not.
Same, and the file most likely to hold a sentence nobody thinks of as copy.

No extractor claims it, so the residual sweep reads the whole file and finds nothing human-looking. `scanned-zero` is the honest answer — 'looked at all of it, found no text' — and it must not be confused with `skipped`.
A UTF-8 BOM is stripped before extraction, so every span in this file sits three bytes below its raw-file offset. The expectations below resolve against the decoded text for exactly that reason.
Two-byte line endings. Line and column arithmetic has to survive them without drifting.

Readable but not byte-addressable: a decoded-string offset is not a file-byte offset here, which is why `apply` refuses to patch such a file rather than writing at a plausible-looking wrong place. Being READ is the claim; being patchable is not.
A NUL byte makes a file binary regardless of its extension. Named as such, not lumped in with the extension-based skips.
Past the size cap. It carries text a person could read, but the cap is a deliberate refusal rather than an inability, so it is not flagged for manual verification.
The distinction the `unscannable` bucket exists for: a font carries no message, a screenshot carries the entire UI. Reporting both as 'binary' is how a translated app ships with English screenshots.
A space in the filename. Every path handed to git, to the walker and to the report has to survive it unquoted.
Tracked by git under a directory the walker refuses to descend into. Without directory-level attribution this path is simply unaccounted for and G1 fails with nothing anybody can act on.
Gitignored and tracked anyway, which happens more often than it should. The census has to attribute it rather than call it unaccounted.
Machine-generated and huge. Skipped by name, and named in the report so the skip is a decision rather than a silence.
Following it would pull bytes from outside the repository into a report that claims to describe the repository.

expectations.find: Aucun d'entre eux ne doit finir sans explication.
expectations.why: Ordinary markdown prose in the source language. If this is not found, nothing else in the case means anything.

expectations.find: Construire la documentation avant de publier une version.
expectations.why: A sentence inside an extensionless build file — a place no extension-driven scanner looks.

expectations.find: Les personnes ayant contribué à ce projet
expectations.why: AUTHORS is read as prose, so the line above the names is copy while the names themselves are not.
Resolves at decoded offset 2, not raw offset 5. This expectation exists to prove the BOM was stripped without shifting every span in the file.

expectations.find: Une ligne terminée à la mode Windows.
expectations.why: The span has to land on the text and not swallow or drop the carriage return.

expectations.find: Encodé en UTF-16, comme tout ce qui sort de certains éditeurs.
expectations.why: Found and inventoried even though the file cannot be patched. A tool that skipped it would report this repository as clean while a whole file of copy sat unread.

expectations.find: La recherche accepte maintenant les accents.
expectations.why: Proves the space in the path did not stop the file being read, as opposed to merely being listed.

pathSites.why: The filename is in the source language while the file itself is an unreadable binary. A tool treating every path as an untouchable slug reports this repository as clean; one that renames it breaks every referrer it failed to find. Refusing, and saying so, is the only correct answer.

knownGaps: assets/utf16.md reports claimRatio 0.506 because bytesClaimed counts decoded UTF-8 while bytesTotal counts the UTF-16 file. It reads as 'the extractor skipped half this file' when it skipped nothing. Not asserted here, because writing 0.506 into ground truth would turn a measurement artefact into a decision.

A BROKEN symlink is dropped by the walker before it reaches any skip list, so a tracked one would surface as G1 `unaccounted` with no reason. Not exercised here — the case would fail, and it deserves a fix rather than a pinned expectation.
